clue.text: Calf, perhaps, seen at last?

parts.note: calfskin is one kind of material for footwear, and a cobbler shapes it over a last, the wooden foot model

explanation.surface: Someone spots a young cow, finally, after a long search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calf' and 'last' both look like their everyday senses (young cow, finally), but here calf is calfskin and a last is a cobbler's foot-shaped form.
explanation.definitionFit: Calfskin is a classic material for the uppers and soles a cobbler stretches over a last.

clue.text: Composer left in army

indicators.note: the word in tells us the letter for left goes inside the word for army

parts.note: a host is a great multitude, as in a heavenly host or an army

explanation.surface: A composer was left behind in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was an English composer, best known for The Planets suite.

clue.text: England's openers on ground that is made of clay

indicators.note: in this clue on means the opening letters are attached after the word for ground

parts.note: earth is soil or ground
the opening two letters of the word England are E and N

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen take the field on a clay pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openers' suggests cricket's opening batsmen, but it means the first two letters of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen pots and floors are those fashioned from baked clay or soil.

clue.text: Replies from city shoe-repairer

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: a repairer puts something back together, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Answers come back from a cobbler in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoe-repairer' reads as a cobbler, but 'repairer' is the signal to rearrange SHOE into HOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoes are sounds sent back, so they are replies in a figurative sense.

clue.text: Shark employed on the farm?

definitions.meaning: a large shark with a very long whip-like tail fin
a farm worker or machine that beats grain from the stalks

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a long-tailed shark and the person or machine that separates grain from chaff at harvest.

clue.text: Adventure, making pies to verse

indicators.note: making here means the letters of pies are worked into something new, a rearranged form

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem, a piece of verse

explanation.surface: A tale of baking pies set to poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' reads as baking in the surface, but it is the signal to rework the letters before adding the poem; 'to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is an incident or escapade, one adventure in a series.

clue.text: The hardest thing to drive, but it runs brilliantly in South America

definitions.text: it runs brilliantly in South America

parts.note: diamond is the hardest natural substance
to beetle is to drive in with a beetle, a heavy wooden mallet

explanation.surface: A tough job to steer, but it runs splendidly across South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'brilliantly': this South American weevil has glittering, gem-like scales and scurries along.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian weevil whose scales sparkle like jewels, so it scuttles about brilliantly.

clue.text: Confront Wolves, perhaps, in the mud

parts.note: to face someone is to confront them
wolves hunt in a pack, so a pack is one example of a group

explanation.surface: Taking on Wolves, the football team, in a muddy match.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club, which helps the muddy-pitch picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty treatment of clay or mud spread over the skin, so a mud mask.

clue.text: Settlement on time instead of shuffling?

indicators.note: shuffling mixes things up like cards, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A settlement was agreed on time, though there was some stalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Settlement of particles to the bottom of a liquid is the process of forming deposits.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing lied about redhead

indicators.note: about means the letters of lied are turned around into another order

parts.note: the head of the word red is its first letter R

explanation.surface: A layabout told fibs about a red-haired person.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who does no work is a good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Museum has a thousand in endowment

indicators.note: the word in says the thousand goes inside the word for endowment

parts.note: a heritage is something inherited, an endowment
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A museum boasts an endowment worth a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hermitage in St Petersburg is one of the world's great art galleries.

clue.text: Beyond compare, having no strikers at a?

definitions.meaning: lacking things you strike to make a light

explanation.definitionFit: Unrivalled in one sense, and literally lacking lucifers in the other.

clue.text: Daggers drawn?

parts.note: printers' dagger marks, the dagger-shaped symbols written in text to flag a reference

explanation.surface: Two enemies are at daggers drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daggers drawn' is an idiom for open hostility, but here the daggers are typographical marks that someone draws.
explanation.definitionFit: The dagger symbol used in printing is called an obelus, plural obeli.

clue.text: Calling fellow back totake gin cocktail…

indicators.note: back says the word for fellow is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a man is a fellow or chap

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man calls back his friend to share a gin-based drink.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN turned back gives NAM; 'cocktail' mixes GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Naming someone is calling them by a name.

clue.text: Old wife, in heap, is fading fast

indicators.note: in tells us the word for wife sits inside the word for heap

parts.note: a mound is a heap or pile
rib is an old jocular word for a wife, from Eve being made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: An elderly wife buried in a pile of things is growing weaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moribund is near death, declining rapidly.

clue.text: … purchase from bar before time

indicators.note: before says the word for bar comes ahead of the word for time

parts.note: a lever is a rigid bar used for prising
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone buys from a bar before closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying, but it means grip or mechanical advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase in the mechanical sense is a firm hold giving force, the advantage a lever supplies.

clue.text: Little Polly, say, is darling to embrace a roue

indicators.note: to embrace means the word for darling wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a pet is a darling or favourite
a rake is a dissolute man, a roue

explanation.surface: Little Polly is a sweetheart, hugging a womanising cad.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly is the traditional name for a pet parrot, as in 'Polly wants a cracker'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small parrot is often called Polly, so it is one example of a little parrot.

clue.text: Coming from bath, I dry off-in this suit?

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Stepping from the bath and towelling down, you wear nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the phrase birthday suit, meaning naked, which is just what someone drying after a bath is wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nakedness is jokingly called the birthday suit, as one is born without clothes.

clue.text: This changed circle line in the old days

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of This are altered into a new order

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: The Circle Line was altered back in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route, a handy misdirection here.
explanation.definitionFit: The past, bygone times, is the subject matter of history.

clue.text: Bag Lucy lost, going by air?

definitions.meaning: a small pouch sewn into clothing, a kind of bag
in the nursery rhyme, Lucy Locket lost hers
a patch of turbulence met while flying

explanation.definitionFit: A pouch in a garment, the item in the nursery rhyme about Lucy Locket, and part of air turbulence.

clue.text: Visual changes to the Capitol

indicators.note: changes to means the following letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Alterations are made to the appearance of the Capitol building.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to sight or vision.

clue.text: He received his rents in mid-month

definitions.text: He received his rents in mid-month

parts.words: He received his rents in mid-month
parts.note: rents here are tears or stab wounds, inflicted on the Ides, the middle of March, when a Roman dictator was assassinated

explanation.surface: A landlord collected the rent in the middle of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rents' suggests money paid to a landlord, but it means rips: the dictator was stabbed on the Ides of March.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius was stabbed to death on the Ides of March, so he got his wounds mid-month.

clue.text: Get people in to coach

parts.note: to put passengers or troops aboard a motor coach

explanation.surface: A sports club brings in someone to train the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like training, but it is a road vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To embus is to load troops or passengers onto a vehicle.

clue.text: Isolated chaps, sort of cross and flat

parts.note: apart means separated or isolated
men are chaps
a T is shaped like a type of cross

explanation.surface: Lonely men, rather annoyed and dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' and 'flat' read as moods, but one is a T-shape and the other a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat in British usage is a set of rooms, a home within a larger building.

clue.text: In France, she takes name of Terry

parts.note: elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A French woman takes the name Terry.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellen Terry was a celebrated Victorian English stage actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen Terry was a great Shakespearean actress, so this is her first name.

clue.text: Capital people coming out of Lord's-none running wild?

indicators.note: running wild means the letters break loose and come out in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Crowds pour out of the cricket ground, nobody behaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground; the possessive 's gives just an S.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Britain's capital city are its residents.

clue.text: Instrument for the sitting-bower?

parts.note: a bower here is one who draws a bow across strings, and this player must sit down to perform

explanation.surface: Some music for a garden arbour where people sit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bower' looks like a shady garden retreat, but it is someone who bows, a string player who plays seated.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist sits and bows the large stringed instrument held between the knees.

clue.text: With drooping tubular bloomers, one says very little at factory

parts.note: a tight-lipped person is said to be as close as an oyster, so an oyster is one who says little
a plant is an industrial works or factory

explanation.surface: A quiet worker at a factory wears baggy knickerbockers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' look like underwear, but they are flowers: the coastal herb has hanging bell-like blue blossoms.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside herb Mertensia carries nodding tube-shaped blue blossoms.
